text:
jess: FYI hit a weird one when trying to run redwoodctl in an Alpine-based localtest container. install fails on postinstall symlink step

sam: ugh. is this the musl apk image?

jess: yeah. `FROM alpine:3.18` + node14. `npm install -g redwoodctl` blows up with EACCES creating /usr/local/bin symlink :facepalm:

mike: alpine images often don't have /usr/local/bin owned by node. try `mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && chown node:node /usr/local/bin` before global install?

jess: tried that, still fails during the `postinstall` script which expects a tty for the auth flow. in CI we need noninteractive.

sam: is it the device-code prompt? redwoodctl sometimes starts interactive device flow that writes to stdout/stderr and waits for input.

jess: yep. install triggers a quick auth check that does `redwoodctl login` under the hood. it prompts for open browser unless REDWOODCTL_DEVICE_FLOW env var is set.

ci-bot: Reminder: CI containers must run non-interactive. See docs: https://internal.example.com/ci/redwoodctl-auth

mike: workaround I use in builds: set `REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1` during install and run `redwoodctl login --token $REDWOOD_API_KEY` in a separate step. avoids tty.

jess: that works. also had to add `--unsafe-perm` to npm so the postinstall doesn't drop privileges: `npm ci --global --unsafe-perm`

sam: nice. can we add a note to the quickstart for Docker images? new folks will hit this frequently.

jess: yes. PR started: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2587 (draft)

mike: another gotcha: `redwoodctl local-serve --profile prod` will try to read ~/.redwood/profiles.json and bail if it's malformed. in our containers the default UID/GID sometimes makes the file unreadable. ensure you `mkdir -p /home/app/.redwood && chown app:app /home/app` or run with `--config-dir /tmp/redwood-config`

sam: could we add a `--no-config-validate` flag for local dev? saves fiddly file perms when doing ephemeral tests.

devex-bot: Feature request logged: PDE-412 add --no-config-validate to redwoodctl local commands

jess: another login wrinkle: when running under systemd-nspawn or minimal containers, the default browser open call errors out and the CLI falls back to device flow, but the fallback logs are swallowed. we lost 10 mins debugging.

mike: we should make the fallback log more obvious and print the device code URL up front. small UX win.

sam: agree. also add clearer exit codes for auth failures so CI can auto-retry vs fail the build.

jess: I'll add two small changes in the PR: 1) respect REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN during install, 2) surface device-code URL + instructions if no tty.

mike: test matrix suggestion: add an Alpine Docker CI job running `npm ci && redwoodctl --version && redwoodctl config list` to catch perms and auth during release CI.

jess: added job to branch. runs in ~40s on GH actions.

sam: awesome. once PR lands, let's add a numbered troubleshooting snippet to the devex README for CI noninteractive installs.

jess: will follow up with a short doc and a sample Dockerfile. snippet in case useful:

```
# Dockerfile snippet
FROM node:18-alpine
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates bash
RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/bin /home/app/.redwood && chown -R node:node /home/app
USER node
ENV REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1
RUN npm ci -g --unsafe-perm redwoodctl
# later in pipeline:
# echo "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | redwoodctl login --token -
```

mike: perfect. thanks for doing the legwork. :rocket:

devex-bot: PR merged into main (docs + CI job)

jess: closing thread once docs live. thanks all! :heart:
